topic: What makes a piece of data state in a React component, and how does it differ from every other value inside the component?
hook_question: Why does one counter stay stuck at zero?

shots.speech: Same click. Why does one counter stay stuck at zero?

captions.text: Same click.
Why does one counter stay stuck at zero?

shots.visual: Two phone mocks side by side, each with a counter button; the left status pill reads 0 after a tap chip, the right climbs.

shots.speech: State is the value React keeps between renders.

captions.text: State is the value React keeps between renders.

shots.visual: The title card with the refresh, memory and bolt icons.

shots.speech: Here's the before. Inside Counter, you write let count equals zero. Your click handler adds one to count.

captions.text: Here's the before.
Inside Counter, you write let count equals zero.
Your click handler adds one to count.

shots.visual: A code window showing the plain variable and the click handler inside Counter.

shots.speech: Each render, meaning each time React runs your function, builds count from nothing. Your click changes a number nobody watches. Nothing asks React to run again.

captions.text: Each render, meaning each time React runs your function, builds count from nothing.
Your click changes a number nobody watches.
Nothing asks React to run again.

shots.visual: A tap chip hits the Counter entity card; the connector to the React system panel stays dark with no pulse.

shots.speech: And on the next render, the old count is thrown away. A brand new count starts back at zero. The label freezes.

captions.text: And on the next render, the old count is thrown away.
A brand new count starts back at zero.
The label freezes.

shots.visual: The Counter entity card is torn down and rebuilt, its status pill resetting to 0.

shots.speech: The after uses state instead. Think of it as a value React holds for you, outside your function. It survives the rebuild, and changing it asks for one.

captions.text: The after uses state instead.
Think of it as a value React holds for you, outside your function.
It survives the rebuild, and changing it asks for one.

shots.visual: A system panel labeled React holds the count value beside the Counter entity card, linked by a connector.

shots.speech: You click. The handler changes the state value. React sees the change and runs Counter again. React hands back the new value, so the label shows it.

captions.text: You click.
The handler changes the state value.
React sees the change and runs Counter again.
React hands back the new value, so the label shows it.

shots.visual: A tap chip fires, a pulse travels the connector to the React system panel, then back to Counter, and the status pill updates.

shots.speech: Use State asks React to remember count. React keeps that value between renders. Set Count changes it, and that change triggers the re-render.

captions.text: `useState` asks React to remember count.
React keeps that value between renders.
`setCount` changes it, and that change triggers the re-render.

shots.visual: The code map card linking useState to the React system panel and setCount to a trigger chip.

shots.speech: Same click, side by side. The plain variable stays stuck at zero. The state value climbs, because React remembers it and runs Counter again.

captions.text: Same click, side by side.
The plain variable stays stuck at zero.
The state value climbs, because React remembers it and runs Counter again.

shots.visual: The two phone mocks again; the state counter's status pill now shows a success state as it climbs.

shots.speech: Plain variables are rebuilt every render. State is kept alive by React. Changing state triggers the re-render.

captions.text: Plain variables are rebuilt every render.
State is kept alive by React.
Changing state triggers the re-render.

shots.visual: The takeaway list with the refresh, memory and bolt rows.

shots.speech: Follow at learn the simple way for more.

captions.text: Follow at learn the simple way for more.
